method: Independent integer-nanosecond median/min/max and inclusive linear-interpolation quartiles, all reported ratios, every recorded process result, exact artifact/build/committed-source identities, and before/after cache headers/hashes. Independent validators reused only after their source hashes were verified. No benchmark/statistics helper, compiler, native executable, or timed workload was executed.
limits: Forty-eight measured rounds cover each inventory four-engine permutation twice and each control three-engine permutation eight times; the two warmup rounds and cross-round predecessors are not fully balanced.
Consecutive saved indices, exact expected counts and reviewed no-filter harness establish completeness of these records; no independent OS process log can rule out earlier unrecorded attempts.

The hashed harness compared full stdout and filesystem bytes before storing each result. This audit verifies retained expected bytes and all per-run hashes/lengths/status/stderr; full per-run output file copies are not retained.

TracerPid was sampled at three checkpoints and affinity recorded after pinning, not continuously. Shared-host interference and CPU migrations outside those controls cannot be excluded from records alone.
Bytecode timestamp headers and before/after bytes are verified; the audit does not independently decompile cache payloads. These are warm-cache whole-process runs, not cold import benchmarks.
Rust preserves the eager algorithm and BigInt quantities but uses native containers, borrowed references and direct formatting. No identical-allocation or general language-speed claim follows.
The normal and ThinLTO sessions ran sequentially. Their within-mode matched comparisons are stronger than attributing cross-session changes solely to LTO.
